- One irregular, organic CHUNK OF LAND floats in the middle of a plain WHITE page (#ffffff), spanning about 75 percent of the frame width, with plenty of white around it.

- Small clumps of dirt and root tendrils dangle beneath. Now and then a tiny crumb breaks off, falls into the white and fades.
- The island bobs very gently, as if floating.
- The camera is a FIXED ORTHOGRAPHIC ISOMETRIC view, about 30 degrees down and 45 degrees around. It never moves, zooms or shakes; all the life is inside the scene.
- The edge of the island dissolves softly into the white.

- No pixelation and no dithering: realism changes the rendering, never the framing.
- Physically based limestone and granite blocks, mortar, slate and timber roofs, weathered oak, iron, cloth banners, grass, soil and water.
- One low warm sun from the side with real soft shadows and contact shadows, and a soft sky fill so no shadow is ever black.
- Subtle ambient occlusion, ACES filmic tone mapping and gentle bloom.
- A very subtle fixed tilt-shift blur at the island's far and near ends, so it reads as an exquisite miniature.
- No low-poly, flat shading, plastic surfaces or stained-glass look.

- A tall square KEEP with a crenellated parapet, small arrow-slit windows and a steep slate roof on its corner turret.
- A curtain WALL with a wall-walk, merlons and two round towers with conical slate roofs, enclosing a cobbled COURTYARD.
- A GATEHOUSE with a pointed arch, a raised portcullis and a timber drawbridge over a short moat that runs out to the island's edge.

- Every part is physically connected and supported.

The look is inspired by an ordered-dither style, rendered LIGHTER than a heavy dither: render the scene to a reduced-resolution target (about half resolution) with nearest filtering for a slightly chunky, crafted pixel feel, then a full-screen post-process that applies a subtle ordered (Bayer) dither across many tonal levels (so the dither only shows as fine texture in the gradients, never as a heavy screen-door pattern over everything), keeping the colour: cold desaturated blue-greys for the stone in shadow, warm amber and orange for everything the torches light. Add a REAL TILT-SHIFT treatment in that post-process: a depth-aware lens blur that leaves a horizontal band through the player razor sharp and grows strongly toward the top and bottom of the screen, so the dungeon reads as a tiny miniature diorama; plus a soft vignette and light film grain. Do not use a heavy screen-door dither, bright saturated colours, glossy plastic materials, a clean modern look or a stained-glass look.

Build the dungeon in code: rough stone-block walls with cut-away fronts so the isometric camera can always see the player, flagstone floors with cracks, moss and puddles that reflect the firelight, wooden doors, iron-barred cells, pillars, stairs down, rubble, barrels, crates, bones, cobwebs, chests, banners and a few traps (spike plates, a swinging blade); rooms linked by corridors, with a sense of going deeper. Monsters roam: skeletons, giant rats and a slime or two, each readable by torchlight with a small glow in their eyes. The PLAYER is a small, clearly built adventurer (hooded cloak, armour, a torch held high casting the main light, a sword) with a proper walk cycle, a sword swing with a clear arc and impact, a hit flinch, and a torch that sways with each step. It explores room by room on its own, walks to monsters and fights them, opens chests for gold and potions, drinks a potion when hurt, finds the key, unlocks the door to the stairs and descends to the next, deeper level, forever, so the page is a self-running game to watch. ENEMIES MUST BE PRESENT AND ACTIVE: every room and most corridors hold monsters that are clearly visible on screen (skeletons, giant rats, slimes, and a bigger boss monster on every third level), they notice the hero, approach and attack, and the hero fights them in frequent, readable sword fights with swings, hits, knockback, hit flashes and monsters collapsing or bursting into bones and goo; a fight should be on screen most of the time, never long stretches of an empty dungeon. A small HUD shows health hearts, gold, depth and monsters slain, in a crisp pixel font. Nothing passes through anything it should not: no walking through walls, pillars or monsters. Add synthesized sound with Web Audio: footsteps on stone, the crackling torch, sword swings and hits, monster squeals, coins, a door unlocking and a low dungeon drone; because browsers gate audio behind a gesture, show only a small, unobtrusive "click for sound" hint in a corner that enables audio when clicked; the game itself starts and runs immediately without it and never waits for any input.
